briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Relief in Sight as Federal Momentum Builds
briefs.top: Michigan operators are finally seeing real paths forward on the 24% wholesale tax — a bipartisan repeal push, a landmark lawsuit finally reaching trial, and creative supplier deals are giving retailers options beyond just absorbing the hit. Nationally, a federal court just locked in medical marijuana's Schedule III status, Congress bought hemp retailers another month, and psychedelics regulation is sprinting toward first approvals.

local.text: John James backs cannabis tax repeal — Michigan U.S. Senate candidate throws support behind killing the 24% wholesale tax as lawmakers from both parties back relief bills.
MiCIA's original tax lawsuit finally reaches trial — the industry group's first constitutional challenge to the wholesale tax heads to court this month, opening a real shot at relief.
Jars Cannabis wins removal of surveillance camera — Madison Heights agrees to take down a Flock camera aimed at the retailer's parking lot after the company pushed back.
Muskegon's Fields Cannary targets fall opening — a hospitality-forward dispensary-and-restaurant combo pushes the retail format further than most Michigan stores have gone.
Rize keeps growing despite the wholesale tax — the Upper Michigan chain negotiates cost-sharing deals with suppliers, splitting the tax burden instead of absorbing it alone.

national.text: Court upholds medical marijuana's Schedule III status — reclassification opponents lost their bid to undo April's rescheduling order, keeping easier tax and banking rules intact.
Trump signs hemp ban delay into law — the federal THC product ban is pushed from November 12 to December 11, buying retailers more runway.
FDA lays out new psychedelics review framework — fresh NEJM guidance reshapes trial design and access rules for psilocybin and MDMA therapies, signaling a faster path to approval.
Canopy Growth rolls out new product formats — new pastilles, all-in-one vapes, and softgels expand the lineup as international growth continues.
Trulieve opens its 178th dispensary nationwide — a new Dunwoody, Georgia location pushes the company's Florida store count to 77 as expansion continues.
